method: Static review of all supplied JavaScript, Rizin native control-flow inspection, Cleave facts and decoded strings, upstream source comparison, registry/Git verification, and fetched dependency source review. No sample or npm lifecycle script was executed.

evidence: Main at 0x1e670 constructs Process, dispatches CLI help/version, then constructs App and calls App::exec at 0xceab0. App tests controller readiness and returns 2 via 0xcebb0 when no configuration is valid; successful initialization honors background/dry-run and starts the libuv event loop.
Configuration loader at 0x53160 follows CLI configuration, config.json, .xmrig.json and .config/xmrig.json fallbacks. No embedded mining-pool/wallet JSON was recovered.

Stratum login/submit construction at 0x64144/0x65260 and developer donation setup at 0xe0b80 correspond to upstream source. Donation pools use donate.v2.xmrig.com and port 3333 (0xd05); this is upstream donation functionality.

The kill sequence at 0x1f1020 follows failed setgroups, obtains its own PID and sends signal 9 to itself. It is libc credential consistency handling, not competitor termination. execve at 0x20790c is a linked libc wrapper.

178 decoded candidates were inspected. For example, the XOR candidate at 0x2115aa is ordinary plaintext help, reads=N ... number of CPU t, XORed with 23 by heuristic extraction. No hidden executable was established.
samples.source_label_explanation: Inference: the listed engines detect XMRig/mining/PUA capability. Such miners are often redistributed for unauthorized use, but this standalone configurable executable contains no demonstrated hostile deployment mechanism.

evidence: Main at 0x10cc0 constructs Process at 0x59e40, dispatches Entry at 0x59210/0x592c0, then constructs App at 0xf5de0 and calls App::exec at 0xf5a10.

App::exec tests readiness at 0xf5a33 and returns status 2 at 0xf5b80 when no configuration is valid; the other path initializes the controller, checks background/dry-run, starts it and enters libuv. This matches upstream App.cpp.

Stratum keepalive and job submission around 0x60cd6 and 0x63b2a implement mining protocol operations. CPU/cgroup information and hugepage settings serve worker/memory tuning. No added persistence, credential collection, payload activation or attacker-selected embedded pool configuration was found.
Four decoded candidates are a printf timestamp treated as URL encoding and nonexecutable Base64 candidate fragments; no concealed execution path was recovered.
samples.source_label_explanation: Inference: miner and PUA signatures explain the external detections; mining functionality alone does not establish unauthorized use.

samples.identification: Leo Streams 2.0.0 npm stream helper library
evidence: All six archive files were read. index.js exports batching, buffering, timed flushing, Fibonacci retry, CSV/JSON transformations, gzip/gunzip factories and logging over caller-supplied streams. commandWrap dispatches caller-supplied callbacks from cmd-prefixed options; it does not execute OS commands or evaluate source.

flushwrite.js implements a Writable with an identity-based Buffer flush sentinel and stream end/destroy callbacks. promisestreams.js wraps supplied transform/reduce/divert callbacks and util.promisify(pipeline); it performs no payload loading.

No install hook, networking, credential acquisition, obfuscation or unsolicited process execution occurs in the package. The gzip/gunzip exports reference zlib factories rather than calling them at load time.
The fetched npm tarball has exactly the supplied SHA256. All six files are byte-identical to Git revision fe9b01bbffb215385f576067d40bf2633ee86edc.

Fetched and reviewed declared lower-bound/current-major direct dependency sources, including leo-logger 1.0.1 and 1.0.7, plus selected transitive sources. Logger initialization configures namespaced console output from LEO_LOGGER; stream/CSV/retry modules provide their documented operations. No hostile runtime extension or install hook was established. Build-tool execution and compiler/template evaluation in old transitive tooling are explicit utility functions, not remotely triggered payloads.
samples.source_label_explanation: The queue supplies no npm-specific detection rationale. No malicious behavior was established. Inference: command-named callback dispatch, prototype methods, or a dependency/reputation association may have contributed to a false label; the actual source of the label is unknown.
samples.trait_changes: Move log-like argument forwarding from console hooking to console I/O; rename command-key read as direction-neutral access; add notable gzip/gunzip factory references.

trait_review.forwarding: Matcher, scopes, confidence and notable severity preserved on relocation; name states log-like receiver, not proof of console preservation. The existing suppression exception references the new ID. No ancestor directory selectors for either source or destination were found.
trait_review.mapping_key: Matcher population and severity preserved; subscript syntax also appears in assignment targets. Updated seven YAML consumers and existing taxonomy fixture references.
trait_review.factories: AST member-expression queries match zlib.createGzip/createGunzip exports or calls, excluding comments, quoted mentions and another receiver. The highest claims are factory references, not execution. Ancestor compression selectors add only compression context; final package scan has zero hostile/suspicious traits.

verification.focused_controls: 9 passed, including factory/comment/receiver near misses, forwarding without hooking, actual console replacements, suppression with and without forwarding context, key assignment, and array-literal near miss. The runner copies fixtures outside testdata so test-directory exclusions cannot conceal failures.
verification.atomscan: Re-ran all three supplied sample paths after YAML edits; all exited 0.
verification.final_scan: All three targets have zero hostile and zero suspicious findings.

limitations: Native builds were not verified byte-for-byte against official release binaries; verdicts rely on inspected control flow and comparison with upstream source.
Static review does not establish whether an operator deploying these miners has authorization.

The npm manifest has ranges and no lockfile. Selected fetched versions do not exhaust every historical or future compatible dependency release. Two historical transitive range lower bounds could not be resolved by the bounded source-fetch helper.
Cleave reports partial JavaScript flow graphs. Full source review supplied the missing context.
